title: Euclid's algorithm: remainders, traces and invariants
goal: Find a common divisor by repeatedly replacing a pair with a smaller problem.

prerequisites.text: You can divide with a remainder and read assignments and a condition. while is introduced here.

sections.title: From the task to an operation
paragraphs: The greatest common divisor of 48 and 18 is the largest positive number dividing both without a remainder. 48 = 2 × 18 + 12. The common divisors of 48 and 18 are the same as those of 18 and 12: subtracting a multiple preserves them.

While b is not zero, compute a % b, then set a to the old b and b to the remainder. while means repeat while the condition is true; != means not equal. The temporary variable remainder preserves the remainder before a changes.

For b > 0, the remainder is nonnegative and smaller than b. Thus the second number decreases to zero; division by zero never runs because the condition is tested before the body. The pair’s greatest common divisor stays the same at every step: this is the concrete invariant. We do not use the pair 0,0 here.

sections.title: Find a common divisor by repeatedly replacing a pair with a smaller problem.
trace: Moved to a pair with the same common divisor.
Remainder 0. The next while condition is false.
The final nonzero a is the answer.

sections.title: Change one condition and check the prediction
paragraphs: Set a=35 and b=15. Write both pair replacements before running.

sections.title: When the result differs
paragraphs: Setting a=b before computing a%b loses the old a: 18%18 gives 0 instead of 12.

sections.title: Now solve your own task
paragraphs: Find the GCD of 27 and 18; show the pairs and explain why the loop finished.
Practice contains a separate starter. Predict the result before changing your program. Returning to the example does not replace your source.

selfcheck.prompt: What output follows the specified change? Set a=35 and b=15. Write both pair replacements before running.
selfcheck.feedback: 35 % 15 = 5, so the next pair is 15,5. 15 % 5 = 0; the answer is 5.

selfcheck.prompt: Find the GCD of 27 and 18; show the pairs and explain why the loop finished.
selfcheck.feedback: Compare the output with the readable reference case below. Explain each change using the objects or operations in this topic. The pairs are (27,18) → (18,9) → (9,0), so the GCD is 9. Assigning a=b first makes 18%18 yield 0 instead of 9 and breaks the first transition.

practice.title: Independent variation
practice.task: Find the GCD of 27 and 18; show the pairs and explain why the loop finished.
criteria: Compare the output with the readable reference case below.
Explain each change using the objects or operations in this topic.
The pairs are (27,18) → (18,9) → (9,0), so the GCD is 9. Assigning a=b first makes 18%18 yield 0 instead of 9 and breaks the first transition.
practice.hint: 35 % 15 = 5, so the next pair is 15,5. 15 % 5 = 0; the answer is 5.

terms.definition: The greatest positive integer dividing both inputs without a remainder.
For nonnegative a and positive b, a%b is between 0 and b-1.
gcd(a,b) = gcd(b,a mod b), provided b>0.
A sequence of intermediate states such as a,b and remainder.
